events.type: sector move / AI-infrastructure rally (no company news)
events.summary: STRL rose 7.71% to $563.69 (open $525.25, high $574.90; volume 633,400, 1.19x its 20-day average). No Sterling press release, SEC filing (other than the 5 Oct general-counsel 8-K), contract, or broker rating change was found for the day. The whole AI-infrastructure group rallied on a record day for the S&P 500: tech gains and cooler Treasury yields lifted the index to a record close (CNBC); the 10-year yield fell 5 basis points to 5.27% as falling oil eased inflation worries (Motley Fool); Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue target to about $20bn on data-center demand (CNBC); Google signed a nuclear power deal with Constellation Energy for AI power (Motley Fool, Yahoo live blog). Data-center construction and electrical peers jumped: MYR Group +7.5%, Comfort Systems +4.7%, Powell +3% in the morning session (StockStory via Yahoo), with Comfort Systems reported +6.12% for the day (TradingKey, low-quality source). The broad infrastructure fund PAVE rose only 1.00% and SPY 0.55% (data/prices).
events.why_it_matters: Santi's 5% rule fired. The pipeline labels +5.0 points as company-specific (z 1.11, within normal noise), but the most likely explanation is that the AI data-center builder sub-group (FIX, MYRG, POWL, STRL) rallied much more than PAVE, which holds a broader mix of infrastructure names (inference, medium). Nothing changed in Sterling's business facts that day. Intraday path: STRL opened only +0.37% and was +5.9% by midday on below-average volume (MarketBeat midday note), consistent with a sector/sentiment move rather than a news shock (inference, medium).

why_chain.text: Sterling itself published nothing that day: the newest press release is 5 Oct (general counsel hire), the only filing in the window is that 8-K, and the only rating change found is a quant Zacks Rank upgrade.

It was a strong day for AI-infrastructure stocks: S&P 500 record close on tech gains and cooler yields; Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue target to about $20bn on data-center demand; Google signed a nuclear power deal with Constellation for AI power; the 10-year yield fell 5bp to 5.27%.

Data-center builders moved far more than PAVE: MYR Group +7.5%, Comfort Systems +4.7% (reported +6.12% at the close), Powell +3% in the morning, 'after surging capital spending for artificial intelligence infrastructure ... bolstered demand across power systems, data center construction, and electrical grid buildouts' (StockStory). PAVE rose only 1.00%.

So most of the 5-point 'company-specific' part is probably the AI data-center builder sub-group rallying, which PAVE (a broad infrastructure fund) does not capture, amplified by STRL's high beta. No Sterling-specific cause was published.

Basic driver: investors' expectations for AI data-center building (more data centers means more site-preparation orders for Sterling) plus lower bond yields that day, which make future profits of fast-growing companies worth more today.
Wednesday 7 Oct: STRL -5.24% ($563.69 to $534.13). Attribution: market -0.73, industry -5.24, company +0.72 (z 0.16): mostly construction stocks falling (PAVE -2.49%).

Why the group fell: the 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.35-5.36%, the highest since 2002, before a $39bn bond auction and the Fed's September minutes; Brent oil traded above $101 after attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, raising inflation and rate-hike worries.
Higher long-term rates pressure valuations most 'outside the mega-cap technology names'; STRL trades at a high multiple and moves about 3x the market, so it falls more than the group when rates jump.
Net over the two days: +2.06% vs Monday's close (PAVE -1.52%, SPY +0.31%). The swing up and down was sentiment and rates acting on a high-beta stock; no business fact about Sterling changed.

products.name: E-Infrastructure Solutions (site development and electrical work for data centers and other mission-critical sites)
products.what_it_is: Getting a very large plot of land ready for a data center, chip plant, factory or warehouse: clearing, grading, excavation, foundations, underground utilities, and since the CEC acquisition, electrical contracting.
products.analogy: Before a house can be built someone levels the lot, digs the foundation and lays the pipes and wires; Sterling does that for buildings the size of several football fields.
products.buyers: Data-center developers and big tech companies' contractors, plus manufacturing, semiconductor and distribution builders. Customer names and concentration not disclosed.
products.how_it_works: Project contracts; revenue is recognized as work progresses. Signed contracts sit in backlog; awarded but unsigned work sits in 'combined backlog'.
products.sales: Q2 2026 segment revenue $905.0M (+192% year on year), about 78% of company revenue; mission-critical projects were 92% of E-Infrastructure backlog at 2026-06-30; company signed backlog $4.33B (+116%). Figures carried from the Q2 release; no new sales data in this window.
products.stage: Mature and scaling fast; management has said skilled labor is the constraint (Q2 call coverage).
products.size_for_company: About 78% of Q2 2026 revenue and most of operating income (segment operating income $210.8M vs $28.2M Transportation and $8.5M Building, Q2 2026).
products.competition: Investors group it with Comfort Systems, MYR Group, EMCOR, Quanta, MasTec; on 6 Oct several of these rose together with STRL, showing the market trades them as one theme.
products.why_investors_care: It is why STRL trades as an 'AI data-center builder'; it explains why STRL jumped with the AI-infrastructure rally on 6 Oct.
products.watch_next: Q3 2026 backlog and book-to-burn (Q2: 1.4x signed, ex Stone Ridge), E-Infrastructure margin as lower-margin Stone Ridge work mixes in, any customer delays; big tech capex plans in late-October results.
